about: Step-named mutation registry (ROAD-29). Each mutation is applied to a disposable copy of the package; 'kills' is the check that must stop passing. 'repin': true re-pins the mutated file's sha256 everywhere in src/ (a forgery that keeps ROAD-26 green); 'regen': 'simulate' re-runs the census in the copy and re-pins it (a cheaper or different experiment posing as the pinned one); 'regen' may also be 'rtp-table' and/or 'record', or a list run in order. Since 14 Oct 2026, 'expectExit' (and 'expectVerdict') must hold for a kill; 'also' applies further text edits to other files. 'op': 'rm' deletes 'file' from the copy; 'truncate' keeps the first floor(n·value) records of the array at 'path' ('coherent': every other count in the file that equalled n is set to the new length); 'null' sets 'keys' to null in every record of the array at 'path'. M01n, M05s and M20d (30 Oct 2026): every reveal null, the dataset cut to 80 %, the census deleted; a verifier that throws on one of them prints no row for the check it names, which this battery scores as a survivor, so each must leave its check FAIL with every row printed. 'repinPackage': true (with 'repin') also replaces the mutated file's sha256 in the copy's RELEASE-MANIFEST.json, MANIFEST.md and README.md, so that no pin and no quoted hash can catch the change. M24a and M24b (17 Nov 2026) cover ROAD-24: M24a changes the site-verifier module and re-pins it everywhere, so only the side-by-side run with src/rng.ts can catch it; M24b breaks the module's pin and leaves the module alone.
